This talk will explain the reasons why the creation of superhuman AI would be detrimental and what PauseAI and others are trying to do about it. Joseph Miller a PhD student in Machine Learning at the University of Oxford, he is also the founder of Pause AI which advocates for leaders to pause unsafe AI development until real safeguards are put into place. description:
What if your passion could become more than a hobby -- what if it could become a career?

Tom Huynh shares how a winding journey from the nail industry to professional fishing taught him an unexpected lesson: great educators aren't defined by a classroom or a degree, but by their passion, expertise, and willingness to share what they know. His story challenges the idea that educators must stay at the bottom of the pay scale and offers a new way to think about turning knowledge into opportunity. I have been in the nail salon industry for over 20 years, and more recently took the professional walleye fishing world by storm by being one of the first to use the newest technology to win multiple pro events and championships.  I have taken what I have learned and developed the first ever online fishing curriculum to teach everything I am learning.  In one year, I have enrollees in more than 40 states and 20 countries. title: Fingernails to Fishing | Tom Huynh | TEDxFargo

author: TEDx Talks
description: What happens when your job becomes your identity? “You Are Not Your Job” explores the risks of tying our self-worth too closely to work and how hobbies, interests, and meaningful pursuits outside of our careers can help us build a stronger identity, navigate career change and job loss, and create a more fulfilling life beyond work. Celeste Bell is a former C-suite HR executive turned professor and researcher whose work focuses on identity, work, and resilience. She’s also a 70-time marathoner who has run on every continent and uses serious leisure as a live experiment in what it means to build a self that’s bigger than a job title. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: You are not your job | Celeste Bell | TEDxRaleigh

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if humor is more than entertainment-and actually a tool for healing? Clinical psychologist and stand-up comedian Dr. Kristen Wynns explores how humor can help us create connection, cope with adversity, and build resilience. Drawing from psychology, her own unexpected journey into comedy, and deeply personal experiences, she reveals that a sense of humor isn’t just something you’re born with-it’s a skill we can strengthen. Her challenge: become a little less serious, a little more silly, and discover how laughter can change the way we move through life’s hardest moments. Dr. Kristen Wynns is a child and adolescent psychologist, founder of Wynns Family Psychology, and author of The No Wimpy Parenting Handbook, whose work has shaped parenting and youth mental health for over 25 years. A sought-after media expert, speaker, and stand-up comedian, she blends psychology and humor to help people build resilience, confidence, and meaningful connection. This talk was given at a TEDx event
title: The Healing Power of Humor | Dr. Kristen Wynns | TEDxRaleigh

author: TEDx Talks
description: Stop waiting to feel ready. Discover how facing anxiety, fear, avoidance, and uncertainty creates the evidence that builds confidence, courage, resilience, and encourages personal growth, one unplanned yes at a time. Dr. Michelle Chambers-Rollins is a trauma-informed mental health clinician and professor at UNC–Chapel Hill whose work examines how anxiety quietly governs the choices we make. Drawing on civic training, public systems work, and her book Faith to Win, she challenges people to reclaim agency and move forward even when certainty is unavailable. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The unplanned yes | Dr. Michelle Chambers-Rollins | TEDxRaleigh

description: Exploring the motivation behind good deeds, Logan’s talk investigates how validation can distort our intentions. Logan contrasts his journey with validation against his grandfather, a World War II freedom fighter, who avoided praise, saying “anyone would have done it.” But not everyone did, and Logan unpacks why and what this contrast reveals about the true drivers of moral action. Logan Eliot is a recent graduate from the University of St Andrews with a degree in Economics and Sustainable Development. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

Through her practice visual artist Julie Brook will explore the idea of what it is to be in our element.
Brook makes sculptural work outside responding directly to the landscape and materials to hand. She will speak about her experience of living on the uninhabited west coast of Jura and how this influences her practice today. Julie Brook is a visual artist who works predominantly outdoors on large scale sculptural work. Her work is directly influenced by the many unique environments she has worked in including the west coast of Jura, the uninhabited island of Mingulay as well as further afield in South West Libya, Syria and Namibia. author: TEDx Talks
description: Excessive and chronic rewards trigger dopamine floods and replace natural rewards. This ''high jacking" of the reward circuit leads to interesting changes in motivation that will change how individuals prioritise everyday tasks, value relationships and their expectations of their immediate environments. What is the difference between a negative and a positive addiction? When does instant gratification and memory impairments become problematic? This TED x talk will explore some of these issues and help normalise the notion that addicted individuals were morally weak and/or genetically  predisposed to become dependent on psychoactive substances. Professor Baldacchino holds a variety of esteemed positions including Chair of the World Psychiatric Association (WPA) Addiction Faculty, Scientific Advisor for the European Union Drug Agency (EUDA) and World Health organisation (WHO). His main research interest lies in improving the lives of individuals with a history of substance use disorders
title: Brain changes in addiction | Professor Alexander Baldacchino | TEDxUniversityofStAndrews

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the most powerful force in achieving something great isn’t certainty—but a sliver of possibility? In this inspiring talk, Jamie Aarons explores how extraordinary achievements often begin with a tiny spark she calls “The Glimmer of Maybe.” Sharing the story of her self‑propelled continuous Munro round, she reflects on being driven not by certainty but by the very real possibility of failure. Through storms, exhaustion, and with some incredibly sore feet, she demonstrated that resilience grows one choice at a time—and rarely alone. This talk highlights the power of community and tenacity, and invites audiences to rethink what’s possible when we let the mind lead the body, when we welcome the prospect of failure as a catalyst, and when we embrace the quiet but powerful idea that maybe—just maybe—something extraordinary could happen. Jamie Aarons is an enthusiastic adventure racer, ultra runner, cyclist and kayaker as well as a devoted social worker. In 2023, she embarked on a sel
title: Why I climbed 282 Scottish mountains | Jamie Aarons | TEDxUniversityofStAndrews

author: TEDx Talks
description: In South Asia, climate change is not only reshaping coastlines and crops. It is redefining childhood. When floods, droughts, and heatwaves disrupt livelihoods, families are forced into impossible calculations. For some, marrying a daughter early becomes a way to manage risk, secure support, or enable mobility. Not simply tradition, but survival shaped by shrinking choices. Masculinities, too, are being renegotiated, as work disappears and expectations remain. Drawing on stories and research from the Climate Brides project, this talk reveals how climate shocks remake family life, gender roles, and the bargains through which child marriage is recast as survival. Ultimately, climate justice is about whose futures are protected, and whose are negotiated away in a warming world. Dr Subramanian is a Senior Research associate and BBC- AHRC New Generation Thinker 2025 who works in the School of Global Development at the University of East Anglia. title: Climate Brides | Dr Reetika Revathy Subramanian | TEDxUniversityofStAndrews

description:
Ana Garcia apresenta o teatro não apenas como um espaço ou uma manifestação artística, mas como uma linguagem e uma forma de existir. Segundo ela, todos interpretamos diferentes papéis no cotidiano, escolhemos figurinos, ensaiamos diálogos e improvisamos comportamentos. A partir dessa percepção, Ana defende que o papel mais importante que uma pessoa pode assumir é o de protagonista da própria vida, escolhendo como deseja construir e contar sua história.
Ao recordar sua trajetória como menina periférica, Ana relata que precisou enfrentar a expectativa de seguir uma profissão considerada segura e abandonar o roteiro que outras pessoas haviam escrito para ela. Após reconhecer, durante uma sessão de terapia, que a arte era parte essencial de sua identidade, deixou o curso técnico que frequentava e começou a estudar teatro. Pouco depois, participou de sua primeira peça profissional, transformando a coragem de seguir sua vocação em uma maneira concreta de criar um mundo possível para si.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
May Amorim apresenta a solidão como um problema de saúde pública relacionado à redução das conexões sociais e ao crescimento do uso de tecnologias. Ela observa que muitos jovens já mantêm interações afetivas contínuas com sistemas de inteligência artificial e alerta para um possível ciclo: quanto menos nos relacionamos com outras pessoas, mais perdemos nossa “musculatura social”, reduzindo a capacidade de criar vínculos e aumentando a sensação de isolamento.

A palestrante, porém, evita tratar a tecnologia apenas como ameaça. A partir dos conceitos de tecnoafetividade, amor como aceitação do outro e afeto como aquilo que amplia ou limita nossa capacidade de agir, ela questiona se a inteligência artificial também poderia fortalecer relações humanas. Embora a ferramenta não experimente sentimentos, o vínculo percebido pelo usuário pode ser verdadeiro. Além disso, habilidades desenvolvidas nessas interações podem ser transferidas para relacionamentos entre pessoas.

May exemplifica essa
title: Tecnologia: um potencializador das relações humanas? | Mayara Amorim | TEDxGoiânia

author: TEDx Talks
description:
One of the biggest diseases affecting leadership today is disease of importance.
People become successful and suddenly become inaccessible.
They become powerful and suddenly become rude.
They acquire wealth and suddenly become superior.
The world does not need more important people. It needs more good people.
People who choose kindness, courage, integrity, service and who refuse to lose themselves.
And if enough of us make that choice, we won’t just change our communities and our countries.
We will change the world. Hon. Zainab Buba Galadima is an entrepreneur, poet, retired politician and an advocate for inclusive leadership. With academic and professional experience spanning Nigeria and the United Kingdom, she has served in various public and private sector roles, including as Technical Assistant to former Vice President Prof. Yemi Osinbajo and as an elected councillor and Minority Leader under the Abuja Municipal Area Council.

A multiple-degree holder with master's qualifications
title: I Refuse to Lose Myself | Zainab Buba Galadima | TEDxSamaru

description:
When Yidan Xu's father was diagnosed with advanced chronic kidney disease in 2023, she came to see that the real issue wasn't the absence of testing tools — it was that people simply weren't getting tested. So as a designer, she created Urify: a kidney disease early-warning system built into toilet cleaning products. With these everyday, low-barrier items, she transforms “treatment after the fact” into “prevention in daily life.”
2023年，徐一丹的父亲确诊慢性肾病中晚期——这让她意识到，问题不在于检测技术的缺失，而在于“检测行为本身没有发生”。作为设计师，她把答案做成了Urify：一款融入马桶清洁产品的肾病预警设计，用低门槛的日常物品，把疾病“事后治疗”，提前变成“日常预防”。 Yidan Xu is a London-based product designer and innovation researcher, graduated from Innovation Design Engineering at Imperial College London and the Royal College of Art. Her work operates at the intersection of people, science, and design.

title: Why We Miss the Early Signs of Illness | Yidan Xu | TEDxNew Channel Qingdao
